content.what_it_is: Python/NumPy/Matplotlib script that loads an inlet-shoal depth matrix from one hard-coded path (L3-L10), interprets its shape as y rows by x columns and builds zero-origin 2 m axes (L12-L18), defines fixed sponge and wavemaker polygons (L20-L25), creates a 6-by-5 inch 200-dpi pseudocolor bathymetry plot (L28-L41), overlays and labels the two regions (L43-L51), and saves inlet__shoal_bathy.png (L53-L54).
entities: np module alias imported at L4
plt module alias imported at L5

equations.expr: x = np.asarray([float(xa)*dx for xa in range(m)])
y = np.asarray([float(ya)*dy for ya in range(n)])

calls: range, float, and np.asarray at L17-L18
unresolved: Execution-stopping API mismatch: L41 calls plt.hold(True), but the script imports pyplot directly at L5 and defines no hold shim. This legacy call is absent in modern Matplotlib, so execution can raise AttributeError before overlays, colorbar, and save at L44-L54; plotting already holds by default and the call is unnecessary.

Likely copy/paste path defect: every title/comment/output describes inlet_shoal (L1 and L54), while the hard-coded input directory at L10 is named Intel_Shoal. If the directory follows the case name, the only input fails before plotting.

Producer/consumer orientation mismatch with mkxyz_shoal_inlet_Uchannel.f: this script maps loaded rows to y and columns to x at L13-L18, but that generator writes dep_shoal_inlet.txt with outer i rows and inner j columns. The plot at L37 therefore swaps the generated physical axes and also discards its centered/shifted coordinates.
Range assumptions are unchecked: overlays require x through 260 at L21-L25 and labels use y=1000 and 1200 at L45/L47, but no comparison with x/y bounds occurs before plotting.
The hard-coded user-specific absolute path at L10 has no argument, configuration, or existence check; the double underscore in the output name at L54 is not explained by the file.
